(2) A further increase in worldwide energy consumption as HVAC systems become more widespread. Overall VC efficiencies appear not to have a path toward stepwise improvements unless heat exchanger size is increased dramatically. In addition; noise, vibration, weight, lack of modularity, and limited portability act as drivers for seeking alternative forms to VP refrigeration and cooling. Thermoelectric cooling is the most pervasive Not In Kind (NIK) cooling technology, finding applications as diverse in use as portable refrigeration to luxury seat cooling. Unfortunately, the application of thermoelectric based cooling to widespread aerospace, automotive, residential, or commercial building HVAC systems has not been economically or technically viable because the electrical-to-thermal conversion efficiencies at temperatures 10- 15C above ambient for even the very best thermoelectric materials is only ~5%. In answer to this need, electrocaloric based cooling has rapidly emerged as a potential form of NIK solid state refrigeration that might credibly offer an alternative to vapor compression based HVAC. Electrocaloric based regenerative cooling, exploits the class of caloric materials which undergo phase transitions between an electrically centrosymmetric phase having no inherent electric dipole moment, to one in which a spontaneous electric polarization occurs as a result of reducing the temperature below a critical, or “Curie” temperature. Ceramics or single crystals, such as lead magnesium niobate system (PMN) and (Pb,Nb)(Zr,Sn,Ti)O , have displayed large electrocaloric temperature lift. However, these 3 7 DE-EE0009099 inorganic materials contain a large amount of lead, which is increasingly disfavored for use in technological systems due to more stringent environmental directives.4 Among all of the EC materials that are promising working bodies for caloric-based technologies,7 polyvinylidene homopolymers, copolymers, and terpolymers have become well-developed in this field due to their large temperature cooling per volt and their scalability in size and shape.5 Relaxor ferroelectric polymers like poly(vinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene- chlorofluoroethylene) (PVDF-TrFE-CFE) have been recognized as one of the most promising candidate materials for electrocaloric cooling due to the polymer’s large temperature change (∆T) that occurs near room temperature with high thermal stability.8–10 In addition, the degree of crystallinity of the polymer is also correlated with the EC effect, which has referred to the entropy changes from the ordering and disordering of the dipoles in the polymers under an electric field.11 Thermal annealing of a PVDF-TrFE-CFE terpolymer has been shown to alter the degree of crystallinity12 and crystal size,11,12 and recently it was found that the EC effect increased as the polymer crystal size decreased13 and degree of crystallinity increased.14,15 The decrease in the crystal size can lower the energy barrier for the transition between ordering and disordering and the increase in the crystallinity can encourage the entropy changes to enhance the ∆T according to Equation 1 from EC theory that is derived from the Maxwell relation. ∆𝑇 ≅ 𝑇1(𝑆(𝑇 ,𝐸 )−𝑆(𝑇 ,𝐸 )) (Eqn. 1), 𝐸𝐶𝐸 1 1 2 2 𝐶𝑒 where S is the entropy of the system, T is the temperature, E is
